instruction: Create a folder named 'backup' on the Desktop and copy all photos from the 'IDS LLM seminar' folder into it.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened the IDS LLM seminar folder, viewed photos, created a 'presenter' subfolder, copied 5 photos (incorrectly including DSC00454 which is a different person), then attempted to zip but the zip command only captured the directory entry without files. The zip was also created inside the seminar folder instead of on the Desktop.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate file manager, view images, create folders, select and move/copy files, open terminal, run basic shell commands (mkdir, cp, zip, ls)
metadata.failure_analysis: Two failure modes: (1) Incorrect photo selection - included DSC00454 (a different presenter, not Tao Yu) in the presenter folder. (2) Broken zip command - ran 'zip presenter.zip presenter' from inside the seminar folder which only zipped the directory entry, not the actual files inside it. The zip was also placed inside the seminar folder rather than on the Desktop as expected.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a pure file copying task with no image recognition required. Tests folder creation and file copying which the model demonstrated ability to do.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a 'backup' folder on Desktop and copying all 6 photos into it. Evaluator lists files in the backup folder and checks all 6 photos are present. Partial credit per file (each worth 1/6).

scoring_breakdown.each_file: 1/6 per correct file present in backup folder

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly lists files in /home/user/Desktop/backup using ls -1, returning structured dict with files list and exists flag
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_files') without incorrectly unwrapping rules
All 6 photos from the source folder are listed in expected_files, providing complete coverage of the instruction
Folder creation is implicitly verified — if backup folder doesn't exist, getter returns exists=False and metric returns 0.0
Partial credit scoring is correct: each file contributes 1/6 of the total score
No postconfig needed — file system state is persistent and doesn't require UI interaction to verify
